content.comment_body: Hello, I am trying to deploy [product_name] Web Editor on AWS, but I am facing an issue where the environment's health status always shows as red. Rebuilding the environment does not resolve the problem. The [product_name] URL is created, but I am unable to control the relays of [product_name] [version_no]. Do you have any advice for solving this? Thank you for your support.

Hi, If you started with a new AWS account, you need to manually configure the environment in AWS. Check this video tutorial: [url] To control [product_name] outputs via the cloud, follow these guidelines: 1. You can control any [product_name] output if it is not part of the [product_name] program. 2. If the output is included in the [product_name] program, you must add an AND/OR condition. See the attached image for more details.

Hello [user_name], Thanks for your suggestions. I have completed those steps. Previously, I was able to deploy the project to AWS. However, I noticed the "AWSElasticBeastalk" policy was removed from my account. I tried using [BINARY_DATA_REMOVED] as an alternative. The issue occurs during the final deployment step of [product_name] Web Editor to AWS—the environment does not get created on Elastic Beanstalk and the health status turns red.

Hi, I had the same problem and suspected it was due to the platform version of Elastic Beanstalk (Tomcat with Java 8 on Amazon Linux) being deprecated. Following advice from a colleague, I switched the deployment to the eu-central-1 region (Frankfurt), which solved the issue for me.

analysis.insight_summary: Users deploying [product_name] Web Editor to AWS via Elastic Beanstalk face persistent environment setup failures. This results in an unhealthy environment (red status) and inability to control [product_name] outputs. The deployment had worked previously, but issues started after AWS policy changes and potential platform version deprecation. Troubleshooting is hard because system feedback is limited, and challenges are compounded by region and version dependencies.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a smooth and successful deployment of [product_name] Web Editor on AWS, with reliable cloud-based control of [product_name] relays, and minimal need to troubleshoot AWS configuration or policy-related problems.
